name: Tennessee Technological University
academic_ranking: Tennessee Tech is a public research university (Carnegie R2: Doctoral Universities - High research activity) in Cookeville, TN, founded in 1915. Enrollment is roughly 10,700 students (fall 2025). It is known for strong engineering, technology, computer science and other STEM programs, and also offers business, nursing, education, agriculture, and liberal arts. U.S. News & World Report ranked it #288 (tie) among National Universities.
financial_aid: Tennessee Tech uses a flat-rate tuition model (pay tuition only up to 12 hours/semester; additional hours are free). Full-time tuition and mandatory fees run about $5,963/semester in-state and $8,063/semester domestic out-of-state (roughly $11,926 and $16,126 annually; international out-of-state is higher). Aid includes the Presidential Scholars program for freshmen, the Flight to Tech Scholarship for transfers (3.0+ GPA, 12+ transferable hours), the HOPE Scholarship, Tennessee Tech Promise, grants, loans, and Federal Work Study. FAFSA School Code 003523. Rates are subject to yearly change. Source: tntech.edu financial aid / paying for college page, checked 2026-07.
